Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) said, "In comparison to the knowledge of Umar (RA), the knowledge of all other people seems like it could be buried in a little hole." [^2]

A man from Madinah said, "When I was presented before Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), learned scholars appeared to be little children before him. His understanding and knowledge towered above theirs." [^3]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Declares that Hadhrat Ali (RA) was the most learned of the Sahabah (RA) and the statement of Hadhrat Ali (RA) about his Knowledge of the Qur'aan

Hadhrat Abu Is'haaq narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ got Hadhrat Ali (RA) married to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), she said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "You have married me to a man whose eyesight is weak and whose stomach is big." Rasulullaah ﷺ responded by saying, "I have married you to him because from all my companions, he was the first to accept Islaam, he has the most knowledge and is the most tolerant." [^4]

Another narration states that Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Faatima (RA), "Are you not pleased that I have married you to the person who was the first of my Ummah to accept Islaam, is the one with the most knowledge and is the most tolerant?" [^5]

Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "By Allaah! I know precisely about what every verse of the Qur'aan was revealed, where it was revealed and concerning whom it was revealed. My Rabb has blessed me with a perceptive heart and an eloquent tongue." [^6]
Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to seek Allaah's protection against any intricate problem which had to be resolved without the help of Hadhrat Ali (RA). [^7]
The Knowledge of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA)

Hadhrat Masrooq narrates that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "I know the precise circumstances surrounding the revelation of every chapter of the Qur'aan. If I knew of a person more knowledgeable than myself, I would certainly go to him if a camel or any other conveyance could take me to him."
